title: FAR Module 5 · TBS 2

fields.label: 4. Contribution Revenue Recognized When Condition Is Satisfied
5. After Recognition: Enter 1 if With Donor Restrictions, 0 if Without Donor Restrictions

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Contribution Recognition Analysis

Analyze a conditional contribution before and after the required barrier has been substantially overcome.

Scenario

Bright Future Foundation receives $180,000 cash from a donor on January 1.

Under the agreement:

  • Bright Future must provide job-training services to at least 600 qualifying participants.
  • If the target is not achieved, the donor may require the $180,000 to be returned.
  • At June 30, only 350 participants have been served.
  • By December 31, Bright Future has served 650 participants and has substantially overcome the required barrier.
  • Once earned, the donor requires the resources to be used only for workforce-development programs.

Required

1. Contribution Revenue Recognized at January 1
2. Liability Reported at January 1
3. Contribution Revenue Recognized at June 30
4. Contribution Revenue Recognized When Condition Is Satisfied
5. After Recognition: Enter 1 if With Donor Restrictions, 0 if Without Donor Restrictions
explanation:
January 1

Bright Future received cash, but the measurable service barrier had not yet been satisfied.

The donor also has a right of return.

Contribution Revenue = $0 Liability = $180,000

June 30

Only 350 of the required 600 participants have been served.

The required barrier therefore has not yet been substantially overcome.

Contribution Revenue = $0

December 31

Bright Future has served 650 participants and substantially overcome the required contribution barrier.

Contribution Revenue = $180,000

Donor Restriction

Once the contribution is recognized, the donor still requires the resources to be used for workforce-development programs.

WITH DONOR RESTRICTIONS Correct Entry = 1

CPA Takeaway

  • Barrier + right of return → conditional contribution.
  • Cash received before satisfaction → generally a liability.
  • Barrier substantially overcome → recognize contribution revenue.
  • After recognition, separately evaluate donor restrictions.
